structured_output.hypothesis: If Darwin is right, then virtually no strictly freshwater fish species is native to the fresh waters of two distant continents, while within single continents many species are shared between some river basins and absent from others.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Using native-only FishBase records, restrict to strictly freshwater species (exclude diadromous, amphidromous, euryhaline and marine-visiting species, and all introduced or established-alien records). Part A: the fraction of these species native to two or more of the continental blocks Africa, South America, North America, Eurasia, Australia/Oceania is <=1.0%, which is the maximum allowed for a claim of 'never' given taxonomic and data noise. Part B: for river basins or countries within a single continent, at least 50% of basin pairs sharing at least one species have a Jaccard similarity strictly between 0.0 and 1.0. In other words, partial overlap is the norm. The claim passes only if both parts hold.
structured_output.fail_criterion: Part A fails if more than 1.0% of strictly freshwater native species occur natively on two or more distant continental blocks. This is still checked after removing records flagged as questionable or introduced. Part B fails if fewer than 50% of within-continent basin pairs with any overlap show partial overlap. That would mean either no sharing or uniform sharing, so range was not 'wide and irregular'. Failing either part refutes the claim as stated.
structured_output.interpretation: 'Fresh-water fish' means strictly freshwater fishes, i.e. FishBase primary and secondary freshwater species, with diadromous and euryhaline species excluded because Darwin was discussing dispersal across land and water barriers. 'Distant continents' are continental blocks separated by ocean, for example Africa vs South America, or Eurasia vs North America. 'Same species' means the currently accepted species name in FishBase. This is a modern taxonomic reinterpretation: many nominal 19th-century species have been split or lumped. 'Range widely and capriciously' is measured as partial overlap of species lists between river basins or countries within one continent, using Jaccard similarity. 'Occur' means native occurrence. Introduced populations, such as carp or trout carried by humans after 1859, are excluded because they are not natural distribution.

dataset.why_it_fits: FishBase records each fish species' environment (freshwater, brackish, marine, diadromous), country and FAO-area occurrence, and a native, introduced or endemic status per country. Fields to use: Species, FW/Environment flags, country checklist (Country, Status = native/endemic/introduced), and river-basin or ecosystem tables. These let me derive a native continent set per species and per-basin species lists. Tables are available via the rfishbase R package, the public FishBase parquet/API releases, and website queries.
